newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares strong into holiday.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares strong into holiday.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 0.52 percent on Tuesday, the last session before Christmas, and market participants forecast that the upward trend would continue into next year.
The 10-share SBI index finished 6.03 points ahead at 1,166.0.
"I expect shares, especially those of newly privatised firms to rise over the first month of next year," Urban Belic, a trader at brokerage Ilirika said.
Turnover climbed to 337.2 million tolars from 226.8 million. Overall 10 shares rose, nine fell and two were unchanged, while another four were untraded.

Bank SKB, which plans a listing on the London Stock Exchange, had the highest turnover. Its shares eased 0.10 percent to 41,710 tolars on volume of 2,724 shares for total turnover of 113.8 million tolars.
Traders were bullish on the long-term outlook for SKB.
"I think SKB's price could exceed 60,000 tolars once it is listed abroad," Belic said.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska bank were the biggest gainer, jumping 9.91 percent to 12,090 tolars on volume of 104 shares.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, falling 10 percent to 7,200 tolars on volume of 196 shares
The Ljubljana Stock Exchange will reopen on Monday, December 30. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
